claimed_mechanism: This architecture strictly implements the scale-split theorem by separating the MOND kernel from the kinetic gapper using two distinct spatial elliptic operators. The auxiliary chi field generates the nonlocal F+ kernel via the (−D²)⁻¹ operator, while the auxiliary s field generates a massive gapper with an operator structurally different from the kernel. The preferred-frame vector u_mu is coupled to the acceleration with a strictly screened coefficient (1−μ), ensuring it only sources the necessary off-ray lensing correction in the MOND regime. The kinetic normalization of the physical modes is governed by the independent s-field mass gap, completely decoupled from the e^-y screening factor, thereby evading the P7 strong-coupling wall.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is genuinely inequivalent to DC-001 and DC-012/013 because it explicitly includes a timelike-background vector field (u_mu) that serves as the preferred-frame carrier, which is mandated by the slip-lock theorem for correct MOND lensing. It is inequivalent to DC-011 because it strictly implements the two-auxiliary scale-split structure, where the operator gapping the extra mode (built from s) is structurally different from the operator building the F+ kernel (built from chi). It is inequivalent to the killed khronometric SEED (DC-010) and FM-000004 because the kinetic normalization source is explicitly 'independent' (sourced from the unscreened s-field mass gap), ensuring that the PPN-visible screened coupling (e^-y) does not control the propagating-mode kinetic normalization, thus bypassing the P7 collision.
name: Two-Scale Elliptic Kinetic-PF Decoupling (TSEKPD)
predicted_weak_field: In the high-acceleration limit (y >> 1), the screened preferred-frame coupling vanishes exponentially, recovering the exact GR limit with c_T=1 and zero preferred-frame PPN violations. In the low-acceleration limit (y << 1), the nonlocal kernel enforces the exact MOND force law, while the un-screened kinetic mass gap from the s-field provides a finite, non-vanishing normalization for the propagating modes. The u_mu field generates the required Φ=Ψ lensing slip without introducing a massless pole, as its propagation is dynamically controlled by the finite s-field mass rather than the screening factor.
